name: Iris Lake
summary: In north-central Ashenvale, Iris Lake lies east of Astranaar, its waters turned yellow-green by corruption from Felwood. Bog beasts prowl its shores.

sections.title: A Tainted Refuge
sections.body: Iris Lake lies between Astranaar and the moonwell tended by Shael'dryn, its waters fouled since the Third War. Fel energies drift south from the tainted heights of Felwood and poison the basin, turning clear water into a yellow-green mire. The corruption has twisted the native plants and water spirits, and aggressive bog beasts lash out at travelers who come near.

sections.title: Tears of the Goddess
sections.body: Pollution chokes Iris Lake, yet sacred remnants of the past linger along its edges. Rare crystalline stones called Elune's Tears sometimes rest on the muddy banks. Keepers of elven traditions, including Shael'dryn, seek the holy stones to help purify tainted moonwells and resist the demonic blight spreading across Ashenvale.

faq.q: Why is the water at Iris Lake green and murky?
faq.answer: Demonic corruption from neighboring Felwood has tainted Iris Lake. The dark magic poisons the water, turning it yellow-green and twisting nearby wildlife into aggressive creatures.

faq.q: What creatures roam around Iris Lake?
faq.answer: Corrupted bog beasts roam the lake and its shores. Fel energy has maddened these creatures of plant and mud, and they attack anyone who approaches the water.
Elune's Tears are sacred blue stones found near Iris Lake's shores. Night elf priests and keepers use them in purification rites, especially to cleanse corrupted moonwells.

aliases: how to get to iris lake
faq.answer: Iris Lake lies in north-central Ashenvale, directly east of Astranaar and west of Shael'dryn's moonwell.

angles.text: Iris Lake shows the corruption threatening Ashenvale. Finding Elune's Tears along its fouled shores offers hope of cleansing the forest.
The twisted bog beasts and corrupted waters show the harm demonic energy brings to nature when left unchecked.
